newsitem.title: USA: U.S. agencies unveil crackdown on pension fraud.
newsitem.headline: U.S. agencies unveil crackdown on pension fraud.

text.p: Attorney General Janet Reno and Labour Secretary Alexis Herman said Thursday an eight-month crackdown on pension fraud has resulted in 70 criminal cases nationwide involving more than $90 million in losses.

They told a Justice Department news conference that 109 individuals had been charged or convicted under the initiative aimed at placing greater emphasis on criminal prosecution of pension plan abuses.

"Most plans are honestly managed and they are sound," Herman said. "A few unscrupulous persons, however, still see these plans as ripe targets to siphon off the hard-earned retirement money of American workers."
Most of the cases involved owners and officials of small or mid-sized companies who embezzled employee pension plan assets for their personal use or for their companies, officials said.
U.S. Attorney Donald Stern of Boston, where five cases were filed Thursday, said prosecutors had been seeking criminal sentences as well as restitution of any money that had beenb taken.

He said one case involved a roofing company owner charged with embezzlement, failing to make required pension contributions, falsifying records by underreporting how much employees worked and bribing union officials to cover up the scheme.
